executive.label: Review conclusion
executive.bottom_line: The portfolio returned 8.4% over the year to 2026-06-30, 0.6pp behind the policy benchmark [S4]. Historical attribution identifies public-equity selection as the largest negative effect for the review period [S5]. All allocation bands remain compliant, while private assets and manager concentration are on watch [S3]. Realized volatility was 9.1%, and the forward assumptions indicate a 6.2% expected return with 10.4% expected volatility [S4][S8].

blocks.title: At a glance
rows: Trailing 1Y return is 0.6pp below the policy benchmark [S4].
Public-equity selection is the largest negative effect for the review period [S5].
All allocation bands remain inside their governed ranges [S3].
Realized volatility is below the benchmark; the private-assets risk contribution is the largest [S4][S7].
Daily-to-quarterly assets cover 63.0% of NAV; unfunded commitments equal 9.3% [S3].
The largest manager is 12.8% of NAV against a 15.0% policy limit [S3][S6].

blocks.title: Scope of this review
blocks.text: This monitoring report provides sourced analysis and considerations for discussion. It does not contain investment recommendations, trades, allocation changes, manager actions or proposed votes.

blocks.title: Key judgment — headline signal
blocks.text: Observation: The fictional TEST report carries a 2 policy items on watch signal [S1]. Why it matters: The signal frames the review. Uncertainty: Evidence coverage is bounded. What would change the view: New governed evidence that changes the signal.

blocks.title: Key judgment — primary measure
blocks.text: Observation: Trailing 1Y is 8.4% in the TEST evidence [S2]. Why it matters: This measure anchors the executive view. Uncertainty: The fixture is deliberately compact. What would change the view: A refreshed source with a materially different value.

blocks.title: Key judgment — monitoring priority
blocks.text: Observation: Liquid share is 63.0% in the TEST evidence [S3]. Why it matters: It identifies a monitoring priority. Uncertainty: Supporting detail is limited. What would change the view: Corroborated evidence that resolves or reverses the item.

blocks.title: Form 13F coverage
blocks.text: Form 13F can lag quarter end by up to 45 days and covers long US-listed equity positions only. It excludes shorts, cash, non-US listings and private holdings; reported USD values are not FX-converted against NAV [S10].

blocks.title: Analysis — Exposure amplifies open findings
blocks.text: Observation: Example Manager A represents 12.8% of NAV and has an open medium finding [S6][S11]. Why it matters: A high-exposure manager can transmit an operational concern to portfolio oversight. Uncertainty: The finding remains open. What would change the view: Closure evidence or materially lower exposure.
